metadata.title: Cathie Wood Invests $36.9 Million in Surging Stock

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Cathie Wood's Ark Invest is leaning harder into space, AI infrastructure and crypto while cutting exposure to several high-flying software names, a rotation that highlights where the aggressive growth investor sees the next leg of disruptive-technology upside. SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Circle (CRCL) and Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) were among Ark's biggest additions last week, while Roblox (NYSE:RBLX) and Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) were trimmed sharply. ARK describes its flagship ARKK fund as targeting companies tied to disruptive innovation.
SpaceX was Ark's largest single-company buy in the supplied trade data, with 316,963 shares purchased across four funds for roughly $36.9 million. The buying followed SpaceX's first public earnings report, when revenue jumped 92% year over year to $7.8 billion but the stock initially sold off amid concerns around elevated spending.
Ark has long viewed SpaceX as a core disruptive-innovation holding, with the company combining reusable launch technology and Starlink connectivity.
AI infrastructure was another clear priority. Ark bought about $13.2 million of CoreWeave, $13.1 million of Cerebras and $17.6 million of Nvidia. CoreWeave operates a purpose-built AI cloud platform built around GPU-heavy computing infrastructure, making it a direct beneficiary of rising demand for training and inference capacity.
Crypto exposure also increased materially, including roughly $39 million of Circle and $17 million of Coinbase.
The selling side was equally revealing. Ark unloaded roughly $96 million of Roblox and about $21 million of Palantir, suggesting Wood is harvesting gains or reallocating capital away from some software winners toward infrastructure-heavy themes.
Investor Takeaway On Cathie Wood Stock
The bigger signal is the portfolio rotation itself.
Investors should watch whether SpaceX can sustain rapid revenue growth while controlling capital intensity, and whether CoreWeave and other AI-infrastructure companies can convert extraordinary compute demand into durable cash flow. CoreWeave says it now operates dozens of AI-focused data centers with more than 1 GW of active power, underscoring the scale of the infrastructure buildout Ark is backing.
At the same time, continued selling in Roblox and Palantir would suggest Ark increasingly sees better risk-reward elsewhere. If AI infrastructure demand weakens or SpaceX spending rises faster than revenue, Wood's latest rotation could prove considerably more vulnerable.
